a_gaps.name: Markdown-as-DSL agentic DSL
a_gaps.target_a: OS/workflow/ (would require a fundamentally new authoring layer)
a_gaps.description: gh-aw lets non-JS authors write workflows in NL markdown. workflow requires TS/JS.

a_gaps.name: Multi-engine agent support
a_gaps.description: gh-aw supports Copilot/Claude/Codex/Gemini/Crush with per-engine feature matrix; workflow's AI helpers are thinner.

a_gaps.name: Safe-outputs handler for validated writes
a_gaps.description: gh-aw enforces all write side-effects through a schema-validated handler. workflow relies on author-written zod/types.

a_gaps.name: Built-in agent sandbox (AWF firewall)
a_gaps.description: gh-aw ships AWF (Agent Workflow Firewall) with domain-based network egress controls by default. workflow's VM targets determinism, not adversarial isolation.

a_gaps.name: Secret redaction in logs
a_gaps.description: Built-in regex redaction for GitHub/Azure/Google/AWS/OpenAI/Anthropic tokens in emitted logs. workflow has no such layer.

a_gaps.name: First-class approval gates
a_gaps.description: gh-aw has `on.manual-approval` via GitHub Environments; workflow has hooks but requires custom HITL wiring.

a_gaps.name: Dual-level concurrency control
a_gaps.description: gh-aw caps concurrency per-workflow (issue/PR/branch-keyed) and per-engine. workflow doesn't expose concurrency limits at framework level.

a_gaps.name: Large sample workflow library
a_gaps.description: gh-aw ships 272 sample workflows; workflow has 2 workbench apps plus cookbook docs. Delta in breadth.

a_gaps.name: SHA-pinned supply chain verification
a_gaps.description: gh-aw auto-pins Actions to commit SHAs and validates them at compile time. workflow uses standard pnpm.overrides for a few deps but no automated supply-chain hardening.

b_gaps.name: Durable step persistence
b_gaps.target_b: Outside scope — would require replacing Actions-level durability
b_gaps.description: workflow persists each step input/output so the workflow survives cold starts. gh-aw has no equivalent; retries restart the whole workflow_run.

b_gaps.name: Event-sourced deterministic replay
b_gaps.description: workflow's append-only event log + seedrandom/ULID gives deterministic replay. gh-aw cannot replay a run; a re-run starts from scratch.

b_gaps.name: Typed retry controls (FatalError / RetryableError)
b_gaps.target_b: OS/gh-aw/pkg/workflow/ (would be a new agent-loop retry primitive)
b_gaps.description: workflow ships typed errors for opt-out + programmable backoff. gh-aw has only engine-level max-turns/max-continuations caps.

b_gaps.name: Durable sleep primitive
b_gaps.target_b: Outside scope — Actions substitute is `sleep` step inside a job, not durable across runner shutdowns
b_gaps.description: workflow's sleep survives process restarts. gh-aw would need a different abstraction to match (scheduled re-trigger vs in-memory sleep).

b_gaps.name: Pluggable storage worlds
b_gaps.target_b: Outside scope — gh-aw's persistence is Actions-level
b_gaps.description: workflow abstracts storage behind a World interface. gh-aw is bound to GitHub Actions' state model.

b_gaps.name: Framework integrations (Next/Nitro/Nuxt/SvelteKit/Astro/Nest)
b_gaps.target_b: N/A — gh-aw doesn't target Node.js frameworks
b_gaps.description: workflow has 6 first-party framework adapters. gh-aw targets CI, not application frameworks — scope mismatch.

b_gaps.name: Step-level observability (event-aware replay UI)
b_gaps.target_b: OS/gh-aw/pkg/ (would require a new runtime-state store)
b_gaps.description: workflow's hydrateResourceIO gives a step-aware inspector. gh-aw's observability is job-level via Actions UI + `gh aw logs`.

b_gaps.name: Exactly-once side-effect memoization
b_gaps.description: workflow memoizes successful steps structurally. gh-aw only dedupes writes through safe-outputs handler.
